title: Derived module evaluation is abelian cohomology on the slice
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of associative unital rings, without a commutativity assumption, and $M$ a sheaf of left $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in a common universe containing objects, arrows, coefficients and covering index sets; assume $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. For an object $W$ give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology, and let $M_{ab}|_W$ be the sectionwise restriction of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},W}:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be evaluation $N\mapsto N(W)$, and compute its right derived functors by injective module resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every integer $q\geq0$ there is a canonical additive isomorphism
$$ R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},W}(M)\cong H^q(\mathcal C/W,M_{ab}|_W), $$
where the right side is right derived evaluation at the terminal object $\operatorname{id}_W$ in abelian sheaves on the slice. The isomorphism is natural in $M$ and in degree zero identifies the two evaluations $M(W)$. No injectivity of $M_{ab}$ or flatness of $\mathcal O$ over the constant integer sheaf is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] at the object $W$. Its smallness, common-universe and enough-injectives hypotheses are precisely those of the item; its ring sheaf is arbitrary and its modules are left modules, with no commutativity or flatness requirement. It supplies canonical additive isomorphisms $\alpha^q_M:R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},W}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(W,M_{ab})$, natural in $M$, with $\alpha^0_M$ the identity under the usual degree-zero evaluation identifications.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, second equality and proof

proof.text: Put $G=M_{ab}$. By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] the abelian sheaf category has enough injectives; choose an injective resolution $G\to J^\bullet$ as in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Restriction $j_W^*$ to the slice is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives] and sends injective abelian sheaves to injective abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization]. Thus $G|_W\to J^\bullet|_W$ is an injective resolution: exactness preserves its augmented exact sequence, and every restricted term is injective. This uses an abelian resolution of $G$, not a claim that the forgotten terms of a module resolution are injective.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open (1) and proof; exact restriction and extension by zero: sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI and 03DJ

proof.text: The object $\operatorname{id}_W$ is terminal in $\mathcal C/W$: the only morphism from $V\to W$ to it is the structure arrow. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $\Gamma(\operatorname{id}_W,J^n|_W)=J^n(W)$ and this equality respects both differentials and augmentations. The cohomology definition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] therefore computes $H^q(W,G)$ and $H^q(\mathcal C/W,G|_W)$ by the identical complex $J^\bullet(W)$. Let $\beta^q_G$ be its identity-induced additive isomorphism. A comparison chain map over the identity of $G$ restricts to the same evaluated chain map; hence the resolution-independence identifications specified in that definition agree on both sides. Likewise a chain map lifting $G\to G'$ evaluates to the same map on both sides, proving naturality of $\beta$. In degree zero, both augmentations are the same $G(W)\to J^0(W)$, so $\beta^0_G$ identifies $G(W)$ with $G|_W(\operatorname{id}_W)$ by the identity.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open (2), proof: equality of the section complexes

proof.text: Define the asserted comparison as $\beta^q_{M_{ab}}\circ\alpha^q_M$. Its source and target are the two groups in the statement. It is an additive isomorphism as a composite of additive isomorphisms. For a module morphism $f:M\to N$, the naturality squares for $\alpha$ and for $\beta$ at $f_{ab}$ paste to the naturality square for this composite. When $q=0$ each factor is the identity of $M(W)$ under the evaluation identifications established above. The construction imposes neither injectivity of $M_{ab}$ nor flatness of $\mathcal O$ over the integer sheaf.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-674da8244 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 4 steps in full. The statement is unchanged and correct against Stacks Tag 03FD (sites-cohomology.tex lines 1862-1921) and Tag 03F3 (lines 608-642). No new nodes, no cycle, no SGA. Live and side-live still show the item unsplit with no repair note, so the delivery is not superseded. Step 1: the cited lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison states exactly the canonical, natural, degree-0-normalized isomorphism used; its ring is an arbitrary sheaf of rings (Lean uses RingCat) acting on the left, and its hypotheses match the item verbatim. Step 2: restricting an abelian injective resolution is elementary from two cited statements, exactness of restriction (lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives) and preservation of injectives (lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization); the step does not assume module injectives are abelian injectives. Step 3: id_W is terminal, def-pur-localized-ringed-site gives sectionwise restriction, and def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology(2) gives the resolution-independence maps and H^0 = evaluation, so the complexes are identical and the step is elementary. It re-derives the localization isomorphism only to get the degree-0 identity, which the localization node does not state. Step 4 composes and pastes the naturality squares. Edge cases checked: point site with O = M = F_p (M injective as a module but not in Ab), O = M_2(F_p), M = 0, a site with no final object, and smallness of the slice. The duplicate search found only overlaps: the abelian-only localization node, lem-pe-injective-complex-slice-section-model (derived, constant ring) and det-pe-injective-acyclicity-reduction (commutative Λ). I accept the 3 declared tool_uses as generic site-cohomology facts that replace no step of the unit's route (main-20261015 sk-prop-sf-comparison proof, first paragraph).
